Unit 1 of 10: What Economics Is About; Consumption, Production, Distribution

Key ideas

  • Human wants are unlimited, but resources are scarce and have alternative uses — so we must choose. This problem of choice is the core of economics.
  • Consumer: buys goods and services to satisfy wants. Producer: produces goods for sale. Service holder/provider: works for others or provides services for payment.
  • Consumption, production and distribution are the three main economic activities studied.
  • Economic facts are expressed in numbers (data); statistics helps us study them.

Worked examples

Example 1: Why is scarcity the root of economic problems? Answer: because limited resources can't satisfy all unlimited wants, so choices must be made.

10-mark practice set

  1. (1 mark, MCQ) The basic economic problem arises because: (a) wants are limited (b) resources are scarce relative to wants (c) money is scarce (d) people are poor. Answer: (b).
  2. (1 mark) Name the three main economic activities. Answer: consumption, production and distribution.
  3. (2 marks) Distinguish between a consumer and a producer. Answer: consumer — buys goods/services to satisfy wants (1); producer — makes goods/services for sale (1).
  4. (3 marks) Explain why resources having alternative uses makes choice necessary. Answer: a resource used for one good can't be used for another (1); there is an opportunity cost (1); society must decide the best use (1).
  5. (3 marks) Give one example each of consumption, production and distribution. Answer: a family buying food (1); a farmer growing wheat (1); wages paid to workers / sharing national income (1).

Common mistakes

  1. Scarcity = poverty. 2. Money as the resource. 3. Missing alternative uses. 4. Mixing consumer/producer. 5. No examples.

Quick recall

  1. Wants? 2. Resources? 3. Core problem? 4. Three activities? 5. Service holder?

Answers: 1) Unlimited. 2) Scarce. 3) Choice. 4) Consumption, production, distribution. 5) Works for others for payment.
